name: Zepho
overview: Zepho was a male Edomite chief, known as the son of Eliphaz. He held a position of leadership among the Edomites, a tribe descending from Esau. His role as a chief highlights his significance within the Edomite lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Zepho means "gaze," reflecting a proper name given in the Old Testament. An alternate form, Zephi, appears in the Chronicles but does not have a specified meaning. Neither name was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Zepho is explicitly identified as the son of Eliphaz, establishing his place within the Edomite family line. Beyond this, Scripture does not record other family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Zepho's importance lies in his role as a chief of Edom and as a son of Eliphaz, situating him within the genealogical and tribal history of the Edomites. His mention in Genesis and Chronicles connects him to the broader narrative of Edomite leadership and heritage, underscoring the continuity of the Edomite nation.
